purpose: Pre-RTL LQ / D$ miss-slot sizing study (foundation plan 3.1). Model results, not RTL measurements, core IPC claims or MLP of the current core.
assumptions: Two-wide dispatch/writeback/retire, 32-entry ROB, one AGU launch per cycle (architecture contract D2).
MSHR1 is the blocking baseline cache: no hit launches while a miss is outstanding. MSHR>1 allows hits under misses.
Each miss is a distinct line: no merging. Responses return in ready-cycle order with fixed latency per point.
Target credits cap live miss requests independently of MSHRs; the current memory protocol has one.
LQ entries are held from dispatch to retirement; SQ entries from dispatch to retirement. Committed-store drain bandwidth is not modeled.
Stores are address-ready at dispatch and launch oldest-first, so no load passes an unknown older store; no forwarding or speculation.
ALU ops are independent single-cycle producers that compete for the two writeback slots, oldest first, with load results.
A ready miss without an MSHR or credit holds the AGU for that cycle (replay); dependent loads wait for producer writeback.
